How much does UGC cost? A simple guide for small brands.

By Aurely Made · October 15, 2026 · 5 min read
$

Most brands ask the same first question: "How much does UGC cost?" The honest answer is: it depends on what you need the content to do. Here is a clear breakdown, using my own rates as a real example, so you can plan your budget with confidence.

What you are actually paying for

A UGC (user-generated content) creator doesn't only press "record". Each video includes the idea and the hook, the filming, the editing, and the right to use the content. That is why two videos that both last 30 seconds can have very different prices.

  • The content itself — how many videos or photos you need.
  • The concept and script — a strong hook in the first 3 seconds makes the difference between scrolling and watching.
  • Usage rights — how long your brand can use the content in its own ads and pages.
  • Extras — raw footage, different formats (9:16, 1:1, 16:9), or several hook versions to test.

A real example: Aurely Made's rates

Here are the prices I work with (in USD). Custom bundles are always possible.

What you getPrice
Tester package — 1 UGC video + 1 month of usage rights$50
1 videofrom $100
3 videosfrom $250
5 videosfrom $400
Photos — 3 / 5 / 8$100 / $150 / $250
Usage rights — 3 months / 6 months / 1 year$150 / $300 / $500

Why usage rights matter so much

Posting a video on the creator's page and running it as an ad on your brand's account are two different things. Usage rights give your brand permission to use the content in its own ads and on its pages for a set time. If you only need organic posts, you can keep this part small. If a video becomes your best-performing ad, extending the rights is usually cheaper than producing a new one.

Start with one video, measure how it performs, then scale what works. It is the safest way to spend a small budget.

How to keep the cost under control

  • Start with a tester. One video tells you a lot about the creator's style and how your audience reacts.
  • Order in bundles. 3 or 5 videos cost less per video than single orders.
  • Send a clear brief. Fewer revisions means faster delivery and no surprises.
  • Plan your usage. Decide early where the content will run (organic, ads, website) so you only pay for the rights you need.

Key takeaways

  • UGC prices depend on the number of videos, the scripting and the usage rights.
  • A tester package is the lowest-risk way to start.
  • Bundles lower the price per video.

How to brief a UGC creator (free checklist)

A simple 7-point checklist to brief a UGC creator: your goal, audience, key message, must-show moments, format, deadline and usage rights.

October 15, 2026 · 4 min read Read →
← The UGC JournalTips

How to brief a UGC creator (free checklist).

By Aurely Made · October 15, 2026 · 4 min read
✓

A good brief is the fastest way to get a great video on the first try. You don't need a 10-page document — just answer these 7 points.

The 7-point brief checklist

  1. Your goal. Sales? Awareness? App downloads? One clear goal per video.
  2. Your audience. Who should stop scrolling? Age, interests, problems they want solved.
  3. One key message. The single thing viewers must remember.
  4. Must-show moments. The packaging, the texture, the before/after, the price, the logo.
  5. What to avoid. Words, claims or competitors that must not appear.
  6. Format and length. 9:16 for Reels and TikTok, 15–30 seconds is a good start.
  7. Deadline and usage rights. When you need it, and where it will run (organic, ads, website).
Give the creator the "what" and the "why" — and leave room for the "how". That freedom is what makes UGC feel real.

A ready-to-copy example

"Goal: sales on our website. Audience: busy moms 28–40. Message: our cleaner works in 30 seconds. Must show: spraying, wiping, the clean result, the bottle with the logo. Avoid: comparing with other brands. Format: 9:16, 20–30 s. Deadline: in 7 days. Rights: ads for 3 months."

Ready to start?

Send me your brief through the contact form — or just your goal, and I will help you write the rest.

Key takeaways

  • One goal and one key message per video.
  • List the must-show moments, then trust the creator's style.
  • Always mention the deadline and where the content will be used.

UGC vs influencer marketing: which one does your brand need?.

By Aurely Made · October 15, 2026 · 4 min read
VS

Both make content with your product, both live on social media — so what is the real difference between a UGC creator and an influencer? Choosing the right one can save you a lot of money.

The short answer

An influencer sells their audience. You pay for the post to reach their followers.
A UGC creator sells content. You pay for authentic videos and photos that your brand publishes on its own pages and in its ads.

When UGC is the better choice

  • You run ads on Instagram, TikTok or Facebook and need fresh creatives often.
  • You want content that looks real — like a customer recommending you — rather than a polished commercial.
  • You want to own the content and reuse it on your website, product pages and emails.
  • Your budget is limited and you want to test several hooks quickly.

When an influencer makes sense

  • You need instant visibility with a specific community.
  • You are launching an event or a product and want people to talk about it right now.
  • The creator's personal reputation is part of the value (trust, authority in a niche).
The best results often come from combining both: UGC for ads that convert, influencers for reach and buzz.

How Aurely Made works

I create UGC for lifestyle, fashion, beauty and fitness brands — unboxings, honest reviews, demos and tutorials — and I have also worked as a brand ambassador. That means I can help you decide which approach fits your goal, and create the content either way.

Key takeaways

  • Influencers = reach. UGC = content your brand owns and uses.
  • UGC is ideal for ads, product pages and testing new angles.
  • Combining both is often the strongest strategy.
